title: Cloud configuration: which settings let attackers in, and would you notice if one changed?
short: Check Microsoft 365 and every cloud account against one free baseline this month, block public storage and long-lived keys at the top, and diff the results every week.
answer: This month, run CISA's ScubaGear against Microsoft 365 and a free posture check against each cloud, and fix public storage, long-lived access keys, open app consent and open external access first. Then lock those settings with organization-level guardrails and re-run the same checks every week, so a changed setting shows up as a diff rather than as an incident.
audience: IT, platform and security teams running Microsoft 365 with workloads in Azure, AWS or Google Cloud, in organizations of any size

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Measure against one published baseline this month.
items.text: Run CISA's free ScubaGear against Microsoft 365; it only reads settings[^scubagear]. Defender for Cloud's free Foundational CSPM checks Azure, AWS and Google Cloud against Microsoft's benchmark[^cspm].

items.title: Block public storage at the top.
items.text: Enforce S3 Block Public Access for the whole AWS organization[^s3org], set `AllowBlobPublicAccess` to false on every Azure storage account[^azanon] and enforce `storage.publicAccessPrevention` in Google Cloud[^gcpcons]. Data stores left online without access controls remain among the most common errors in the DBIR[^dbir].

items.title: Replace long-lived keys with short-lived credentials.
items.text: AWS traces a large portion of security events to compromised long-term access keys[^awsssec], and in late 2025 attackers broke in with AWS keys suspected to have leaked in 2022[^th]. Move people to federated sign-in and workloads to roles or managed identities, then delete the keys.

items.title: Close app consent and external access in Microsoft 365.
items.text: Restrict user consent to verified publishers and low-risk permissions, with an admin consent workflow[^scuba]. Allow Teams external access only for named domains: confirmed vishing over cross-tenant Teams calls rose 502% in a year[^mddr].

items.title: Turn the baseline into guardrails, then diff it weekly.
items.text: Enforce what must never change with AWS Organizations policies, Azure Policy and Google Cloud organization policies, then re-run the assessment weekly and compare runs[^scubagear].

blocks.title: Adopt a baseline without breaking things

items.title: Pick one baseline per platform.
items.text: For Microsoft 365, SCuBA, or Baseline Security Mode, which every plan has[^bsm]; for Azure, the Microsoft cloud security benchmark[^cspm]; for AWS, Foundational Security Best Practices[^fsbp]; for Google Cloud, its security baseline constraints[^gcpbase].

items.title: Assess, and write down each exception.
items.text: Export every failing check. Record why each one stays, who owns it and when it ends; ScubaGear's YAML config holds these as exclusions, annotations or omissions[^scubagear].

items.title: Check the impact, then fix.
items.text: Start with the policies CISA marks as BOD 25-01 requirements[^bod], and turn on each Baseline Security Mode setting whose impact report shows zero impact[^bsm].

items.title: Enforce at the top of each cloud.
items.text: In AWS, SCPs cap what roles can do, RCPs what resources allow, and declarative policies set defaults such as IMDSv2[^orgpol]. In Azure, assign deny policies at a management group. In Google Cloud, add the baseline constraints if your organization predates 3 May 2024[^gcpbase]. Test each on one account first.

items.title: Diff every week.
items.text: Compare each run with the last, for example with ScubaGear's `Invoke-SCuBADiff`[^scubagear]. Scan infrastructure-as-code pull requests with Checkov or a similar checker[^checkov], and treat a scheduled `terraform plan` that isn't empty as drift.

blocks.title: Settings attackers go after
items: **Public storage.** Google's public access prevention revokes existing public access the moment you enforce it[^gcpcons]. Move public sites and downloads to a separate account or project first.

**Access keys and shared keys.** Attackers reach Azure Blob Storage with exposed credentials, shared keys and SAS tokens[^mddr]; accounts accept keys until `AllowSharedKeyAccess` is false[^azshared]. Google Cloud blocks service account keys in organizations created since May 2024[^gcpbase] and disables exposed ones[^th].

**Instance metadata.** Require IMDSv2, which uses token-backed sessions, by account default or declarative policy. Find instances that still allow IMDSv1 with the `ImdsV1Enabled` metric, and add `ec2:RoleDelivery` to an SCP so IMDSv1 credentials stop working[^imds].

**Broad roles for workloads.** Remove wildcard actions (Security Hub controls IAM.1 and IAM.21)[^fsbp] and pin GitHub OIDC trust to one repository and branch or environment[^ghoidc]. An over-broad deploy role took UNC6426 from a stolen GitHub token to AWS administrator in under 72 hours[^th].

**Guests and external access.** Let only admins and Guest Inviters invite guests, and only from approved domains[^scuba]. Allow Teams external domains one by one and block chats from unmanaged accounts. Google Cloud's `iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` does the same for IAM grants[^gcpbase]. SharePoint links: see the DLP sheet.

**OAuth app consent.** Microsoft's managed default for new tenants still lets users consent to permissions outside a list of mail, file, calendar and chat scopes[^consentpol]. Changes keep existing grants[^consent], so review those too. Stolen Salesloft Drift tokens exposed Salesforce data at Google, Zscaler, Cisco and others[^dbir].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Exploits overtook weak credentials in Google Cloud.** In late 2025, software flaws opened 44.5% of the Google Cloud intrusions in Google's data and weak or missing credentials 27.2%; misconfiguration fell to 21%. Google thinks its secure defaults explain part of the shift[^th]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines.

**ScubaGear 2.0 is out.** The October 2026 release adds a Security Suite baseline for Defender, Purview, Exchange Online and Teams[^scubanews], and the Entra baseline now requires blocking risky AI agents[^scuba]. Update your config and re-run it.

**Microsoft 365 moved toward secure defaults.** Baseline Security Mode, in the admin center since November 2025, covers admin MFA, legacy authentication and app consent[^bsm]. Tenant Configuration Management, generally available since April 2026, monitors over 200 settings in six workloads[^tcmga].
**S3 public access can be blocked for a whole organization.** Since November 2025 one AWS Organizations policy enforces Block Public Access for every account, including new ones[^s3org].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A paid CSPM before the free checks.** ScubaGear and Defender for Cloud's Foundational CSPM cost nothing[^scubagear][^cspm]. Buy attack path analysis once the basics are closed.
**Perfecting 90-day key rotation.** Security Hub checks for it[^fsbp], but AWS advises not creating long-term keys at all[^awsssec]. Remove them instead.
**A home-grown baseline.** Start from a published one. A list you write yourself has no one keeping it current.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Trusting a new default to fix old resources.** An IMDSv2 account default skips existing instances[^imds], and consent changes keep old grants[^consent].
**Running workloads in the AWS management account.** SCPs and RCPs don't restrict it[^orgpol].
**Exposing a test resource "just for a day."** Microsoft measured a median of 5.3 hours from an exposed container's start to the first exploit attempt[^mddr].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Turn on each Baseline Security Mode setting with zero impact[^bsm].
Ask your IT provider for a monthly ScubaGear report and the list of consented apps and guests.
Block public storage for the whole cloud organization, not account by account.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Run ScubaGear weekly from a scheduled job and post the diff to the team channel.
Connect every cloud account to one posture tool and give each finding an owner and a due date.
Make infrastructure as code the only write path, and keep console write access for emergency roles.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: US federal civilian agencies must meet BOD 25-01's mandatory SCuBA policies and report to CISA[^bod].
Feed drift and posture findings into the SIEM, with a fix time per severity.
Review changes to guardrail policies like Tier 0 code, with two people.
